propositions.text: The principal appellant and associate appellants are Mexican citizens appealing the RPD decision rejecting refugee claims due to an internal flight alternative in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX (principal appellant), his wife XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXand her son, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX (associate appellants) are citizens of Mexico. They are appealing the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) dated December 24, 2019, to reject their claims for refugee protection on the grounds that the appellants had an internal flight alternative (IFA) in Campeche or Yucatan.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants, Mexican citizens, appeal the RPD's rejection of their refugee claims based on an internal flight alternative in Campeche or Yucatan, says the court.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in finding an IFA in Mexico and its evidence analysis was incomplete and erroneous.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege that the RPD erred in finding that they had an IFA in Mexico1 and that its analysis of the evidence was incomplete and erroneous.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants allege the RPD erred in finding an IFA in Mexico and its evidence analysis was incomplete and erroneous.

propositions.text: The appellants ask the RAD to allow their appeal, set aside the RPD's determination, and allow their refugee claims.
propositions.quote: The appellants are asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to allow their appeal, set aside the RPD's determination and allow their claims for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants ask the RAD to allow their appeal, set aside the RPD's determination, and allow their refugee claims.

propositions.text: The determinative issue before the RAD and RPD is the internal flight alternative (IFA).
propositions.quote: The determinative issue before the RAD is the same as the determinative issue before the RPD, namely, the IFA.

paragraphs.summary: The determinative issue before the RAD and RPD is the internal flight alternative (IFA).

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination and dismisses the appeal.
propositions.quote: The RAD confirms the determination of the RPD and dismisses the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination and dismisses the appeal.

propositions.text: The principal appellant, a taxi driver from Guerrero, alleges receiving death threats since 2012.
propositions.quote: On his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), the principal appellant, a taxi driver from the state of Guerrero, alleges that he had been receiving death threats from several people since XXXX XXXX XXXX 2012.

paragraphs.summary: The principal appellant, a taxi driver from Guerrero, alleges receiving death threats since 2012.

propositions.text: In 2013, an individual threatened the principal appellant with a weapon and stole his car.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2013, an individual threatened him with a weapon and stole his car.

paragraphs.summary: In 2013, an individual threatened the principal appellant with a weapon and stole his car.

propositions.text: In 2017, the principal appellant learned a brother came to Canada to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: In 2017, he learned that one of his brothers (XXXX) came to Canada to claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: In 2017, the principal appellant learned a brother came to Canada to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: In 2018, another brother was murdered; the principal appellant moved to Acapulco due to threats.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2018, another one of his brothers (XXXX) was murdered. The principal appellant moved to Acapulco because of the threats he was receiving.

paragraphs.summary: In 2018, another brother was murdered; the principal appellant moved to Acapulco due to threats.

propositions.text: In 2018, two individuals threatened the principal appellant at his home, demanding he leave Guerrero.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018, two individuals came to the principal appellant's house. They threatened him and told him that they would kill him if he did not leave the state of Guerrero.

paragraphs.summary: In 2018, two individuals threatened the principal appellant at his home, demanding he leave Guerrero.

propositions.text: In 2018, the principal appellant flew to Montréal and claimed protection in Canada.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018, the principal appellant took a flight to Montréal and claimed protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: In 2018, the principal appellant flew to Montréal and claimed protection in Canada.

propositions.text: In 2018, the principal appellant's wife left Mexico, joined him in Canada, and claimed refugee protection.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018, his wife, the female associate appellant, left Mexico and joined the appellant in Canada. She also claimed refugee protection, basing her claim on that of the principal appellant.

paragraphs.summary: In 2018, the principal appellant's wife left Mexico, joined him in Canada, and claimed refugee protection.

propositions.text: In 2019, the wife’s son joined the appellants in Montréal and filed a refugee claim after threats at home.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2019, the son of the female associate appellant joined the appellants in Montréal, and he filed a claim for refugee protection on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2019. He alleges that individuals had come to his home on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2019, and asked him where his stepfather was.

paragraphs.summary: In 2019, the wife’s son joined the appellants in Montréal and filed a refugee claim after threats at home.

propositions.text: The RAD reviews RPD decisions with correctness standard, except for credibility assessments where RPD has advantage.
propositions.quote: The RAD reviews RPD decisions, applying the correctness standard of review after carrying out its own analysis of the record. The exception to this rule is where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage with respect to the credibility assessment.

propositions.text: The RAD's role is to determine if the RPD committed errors as alleged by appellants.
propositions.quote: That being said, the role of the RAD is to determine whether the RPD did indeed commit errors, as the appellants stated.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reviews RPD decisions with correctness standard except for credibility; its role is to determine if RPD committed errors as alleged.

propositions.text: The RAD applied the correctness standard in this case.
propositions.quote: The RAD applied the correctness standard in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD applied the correctness standard in this case.

propositions.text: Rasaratnam and Thirunavukkarasu define a two-pronged test for assessing IFA.
propositions.quote: In Rasaratnam5 and Thirunavukkarasu,6 the Federal Court of Appeal defined the criteria to apply in order to assess an IFA.

propositions.text: First prong: no serious possibility of persecution in the IFA area on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: 1. ...the Board must be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that there is no serious possibility of the claimant being persecuted in the part of the country to which it finds an IFA exists.

propositions.text: Second prong: conditions in the IFA area must not be unreasonable for the claimant to seek refuge there.
propositions.quote: 2. Conditions in the part of the country considered to be an IFA must be such that it would not be unreasonable, in all the circumstances, including those particular to the claimant, for him to seek refuge there.

paragraphs.summary: Rasaratnam and Thirunavukkarasu define a two-pronged test for IFA: no serious persecution possibility and reasonable conditions to seek refuge.

propositions.text: Both prongs must be satisfied to conclude an IFA exists.
propositions.quote: Both prongs must be satisfied in order to conclude that an IFA exists.

paragraphs.summary: Both prongs must be satisfied to conclude an IFA exists.

propositions.text: First prong examines agent of persecution's interest and ability to find claimant, then claimant's and locals' circumstances.
propositions.quote: The first prong must be examined from the perspective of the agent of persecution, namely, the agent of persecution's interest in following a refugee protection claimant to the area proposed as an IFA and their ability to find the claimant. Once those aspects have been analyzed, the claimant's personal circumstances and the circumstances of the people living in the IFA location must be considered.

paragraphs.summary: First prong examines agent of persecution's interest and ability to find claimant, then claimant's and locals' circumstances.

propositions.text: The RPD found incidents in Guerrero do not show agents of harm have interest in tracking appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the incidents that occurred in the state of Guerrero (the murder of the principal appellant's brother and the threats made to his parents) do not show that these agents of harm have an interest in tracking down the appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found incidents in Guerrero do not show agents of harm have interest in tracking appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: The RPD questioned why aggressors would look for appellant after he left Guerrero; appellant said aggressors might seek him in Campeche or Yucatan due to revenge or complaint.
propositions.quote: The RPD questioned the principal appellant about why his aggressors would be looking for him when he had complied with their demand and left the state of Guerrero. He stated that his aggressors might come looking for him in Campeche or Yucatan because they think he wants to avenge the death of his brother or because he filed a complaint in XXXX 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD questioned why aggressors would look for appellant after he left Guerrero; appellant said aggressors might seek him in Campeche or Yucatan due to revenge or complaint.

propositions.text: The RPD found the principal appellant's answers speculative and insufficient to show aggressors' interest in tracking appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the principal appellant's answers were purely speculative. The RPD was of the opinion that these factors alone were not enough to reasonably explain, on a balance of probabilities, why the aggressors would still be interested in tracking down the appellants in Campeche or Yucatan

propositions.text: The complaint filed in 2018 does not accuse anyone specifically, only describes threats received.
propositions.quote: since the complaint filed in XXXX 2018 does not accuse anyone in particular. It simply describes the threats received.

propositions.text: RPD did not believe criminals would track appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RPD did not believe that the criminals would be interested in tracking down the appellants in the two locations suggested.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the principal appellant's answers speculative and did not believe criminals would track appellants in Campeche or Yucatan, as the 2018 complaint was nonspecific.

propositions.text: The XXXX family has been targeted for years, attacked by organized crime, and parents still contacted by agents of harm.
propositions.quote: The appellants argue that the XXXX family (the principal appellant's family) has been targeted for years, that they have been attacked by members of organized crime and that the parents are still being contacted by the agents of harm.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue their family has been targeted for years by organized crime and parents are still contacted by agents of harm.

propositions.text: The aggressors' interest changed over time but never lost interest in finding appellants and likely still track them down.
propositions.quote: The appellants argue that the interest of the agents of harm has changed over time... it is obvious that the aggressors never lost interest in finding the appellants and that they are more than likely still interested in tracking them down.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue aggressors never lost interest and likely still track them down despite changing motives.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to justify findings about aggressors' interest in tracking appellants and did not consider all facts or addressed other threats.
propositions.quote: the RPD: did not exercise due diligence in justifying its findings... did not seem to take into consideration all of the facts... did not address the other threats received by the principal appellant and his brothers

propositions.text: The RPD confused aggressors' interest with ability to track appellants, citing incidents in Guerrero as lack of interest in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: did not address the other threats... confused interest with ability by indicating that "the fact that the incidents occurred in the state of Guerrero shows a lack of interest in tracking down the appellants in Yucatan or Campeche."

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD failed to justify findings, ignored facts and threats, and confused interest with ability to track them.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees with the appellants' submissions.
propositions.quote: The RAD disagrees.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD disagrees with the appellants' arguments.

propositions.text: No evidence or testimony identifies the agents of persecution or their interest in finding appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: there is nothing in the evidence or the appellants' testimony that makes it possible to identify the agents of persecution in order to be able to determine whether they have a particular interest in finding the appellants wherever they go in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds no evidence identifying agents of persecution or their interest in finding appellants in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: The burden to demonstrate aggressors' interest in tracking appellants lies with the refugee claimant, not the RPD or RAD.
propositions.quote: the burden of demonstrating such an interest falls on the refugee protection claimant, not on the RPD or the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD states the claimant bears the burden to show aggressors' interest in tracking them, not the RPD or RAD.

propositions.text: The RPD questioned appellants about knowledge of agents of persecution and gang membership; appellants denied knowing them.
propositions.quote: the RPD questioned the three appellants... They responded in the negative

propositions.text: Appellants fear only the unknown people who murdered the principal appellant's brother, no other individuals.
propositions.quote: I'm afraid of the people who murdered my brother... No, I don't know them... No, just those people.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellants do not know or identify the agents of persecution, fearing only unknown murderers of the brother.

propositions.text: The RAD believes agents of harm have no interest in tracking appellants over 1000 km away in Campeche or Yucatan.
propositions.quote: the RAD is of the opinion that the agents of harm have no interest in tracking down the appellants in a location that is very far away (over a thousand kilometres)

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds agents of harm have no interest in tracking appellants over 1000 km away in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: All alleged incidents occurred in Guerrero, including murder and threats to appellants and parents.
propositions.quote: all of the incidents alleged by the appellants happened in the state of Guerrero, whether it be the murder... the threats received by the principal appellant... the threats received by the male associate appellant... or those received by the parents

paragraphs.summary: All alleged incidents occurred in Guerrero, including murder and threats to appellants and their parents.

propositions.text: All incidents were by unidentified individuals for no apparent reason, per appellants' account and testimony.
propositions.quote: all of these incidents were committed by unidentified individuals for no apparent reason, according to the appellants' written account and testimony

propositions.text: Principal appellant's written account describes threats by two individuals warning him to leave the state or face harm.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, I was threatened by two individuals who came to my home... On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018, the two individuals... fired three shots in the air... told me that if I did not leave, then the next bullet would be for me.

paragraphs.summary: Incidents were by unidentified individuals; principal appellant's account describes threats to leave or face harm.

propositions.text: Guerrero is 1,610 km from Yucatan and 1,370 km from Campeche, both on Mexico's east coast.
propositions.quote: The state of Guerrero... is 1,610 km from the state of Yucatan and 1,370 km from the state of Campeche, both of which are located on the east coast of Mexico.

propositions.text: Principal appellant testified aggressors wanted him to leave Guerrero and would let him live if he did.
propositions.quote: The principal appellant testified that all the agents of harm wanted him to do was to leave the Guerrero area and they would let him live.

propositions.text: Moving to Campeche or Yucatan would remove aggressors' incentive to find appellants, meeting aggressors' conditions.
propositions.quote: if the appellants were to move to one of the two suggested areas... it would take away any incentive their aggressors had to find them because they would be meeting the conditions set out by their aggressors.

paragraphs.summary: Guerrero is far from Campeche and Yucatan; moving there meets aggressors' conditions, removing incentive to track appellants.

propositions.text: Appellants failed to prove aggressors have interest in tracking them in proposed areas; their arguments are speculative.
propositions.quote: the appellants did not discharge their burden of establishing that the people they are afraid of have an interest in finding out that they moved to one of the proposed areas. The arguments... are speculative and are not objectively well founded

propositions.text: RPD's conclusion that aggressors lack interest in tracking appellants in Campeche or Yucatan is correct.
propositions.quote: For all of the above-mentioned reasons, the RPD's conclusion is correct.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes appellants failed to prove aggressors' interest in tracking them; RPD's conclusion is correct.

propositions.text: RPD questioned appellants on how aggressors would track them in Campeche or Yucatan; principal appellant did not know but said name would appear on records.
propositions.quote: The RPD questioned the appellants about how the aggressors would track them down in Campeche or Yucatan. The principal appellant testified that he did not know how they would do that but that his name would be on the records as soon as he rented a place to live or requested public services such as electricity.

paragraphs.summary: RPD questioned appellants on tracking methods; principal appellant said name would appear on rental or public service records.

propositions.text: RPD concluded appellants did not prove on balance of probabilities that aggressors could find them in suggested areas.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the appellants did not show, on the balance of probabilities, that these men would be able to find them in the suggested areas.

paragraphs.summary: RPD concluded appellants failed to prove aggressors could find them in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: At hearing start, appellants could not provide information about agents of persecution; principal appellant did not know if they belonged to criminal organization.
propositions.quote: at the beginning of the hearing, none of the appellants were able to give any information about the agents of persecution. The principal appellant testified that these men never identified themselves and that he did not know whether they belonged to a criminal organization.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants could not identify agents of persecution or their criminal affiliations at hearing start.

propositions.text: RPD found appellants failed to show aggressors could track them in Campeche or Yucatan through records or other means.
propositions.quote: the appellants failed to demonstrate that the men would be able to track them down in Campeche or Yucatan, through records or other means.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found appellants failed to prove aggressors could track them in Campeche or Yucatan by records or other means.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD erred by imposing heavy burden to know all details about agents of harm to determine IFA.
propositions.quote: The appellants submit that the RPD erred by imposing on the appellants the heavy burden of having to know all of the details about the agents of harm in order to determine whether there is an IFA.

propositions.text: Appellants argue not knowing aggressors' identity does not mean they cannot be tracked, as aggressors are organized crime, not local gang.
propositions.quote: The appellants argue that the fact that they do not know the identity of the aggressors does not mean that the aggressors will be unable to track them down, since the facts show that these aggressors are very organized, which implies that they do not belong to a local gang but are members of organized crime.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD wrongly imposed heavy burden to know aggressors' details; organized crime can track them despite unknown identity.

propositions.text: Appellants cite NDP showing organized crime acts with impunity, infiltrates law enforcement, and corruption is widespread, supporting likelihood of tracking anywhere.
propositions.quote: The appellants note that the National Documentation Package (NDP) indicates that members of organized crime act with impunity, that they have infiltrated law enforcement agencies and that corruption is widespread to support their argument that it is likely they could be tracked down by members of organized crime anywhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: If returned to Mexico, appellants would leave administrative traces making them easy to find.
propositions.quote: If they were to return to Mexico, they will have to take administrative action that will leave traces that will make them easy to find.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue organized crime's impunity and corruption make tracking likely anywhere; administrative actions would leave traces.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees with appellants' submissions about aggressors' ability to track them.
propositions.quote: The RAD disagrees.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD disagrees with the appellants' arguments about aggressors' ability to track them.

propositions.text: Agents of persecution are members of organized crime in Mexico
propositions.quote: the argument of the appellants' counsel to the effect that the agents of persecution are members of organized crime in Mexico is purely speculative

propositions.text: Appellants did not know anything about the agents of persecution
propositions.quote: The appellants themselves stated that they did not know anything about the subject, and none of them had any information about the aggressors

propositions.text: The argument that agents of persecution are organized crime members is purely speculative
propositions.quote: the argument of the appellants' counsel to the effect that the agents of persecution are members of organized crime in Mexico is purely speculative

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue agents of persecution are organized crime, but they admit no knowledge; the court finds this argument speculative.

propositions.text: Corruption and organized crime exist in Mexico
propositions.quote: the RAD recognizes that corruption exists in Mexico and that organized crime is widespread in that county

propositions.text: Appellants argue agents of persecution have means, ability, motivation to track them in Campeche or Yucatan
propositions.quote: the appellants did not provide sufficient evidence to show, on a balance of probabilities, that their agents of persecution have the means, ability, motivation and interest to track them down in Campeche or Yucatan

propositions.text: Appellants did not provide sufficient evidence to prove agents' ability and motivation to track them in Campeche or Yucatan
propositions.quote: the appellants did not provide sufficient evidence to show, on a balance of probabilities, that their agents of persecution have the means, ability, motivation and interest to track them down in Campeche or Yucatan

paragraphs.summary: The court acknowledges corruption and organized crime in Mexico but finds appellants failed to prove agents can track them in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: The appellants' fear is hypothetical
propositions.quote: the fear expressed by the appellants' counsel is completely hypothetical

propositions.text: The RPD considered the fear but concluded appellants did not meet burden of risk under first prong of IFA test
propositions.quote: The RPD took that fear into account but still rightly concluded that the appellants did not discharge the burden of establishing the risk required under the first prong of the IFA test

propositions.text: The court agrees with RPD that appellants failed to establish required risk under first prong of IFA test
propositions.quote: The RPD took that fear into account but still rightly concluded that the appellants did not discharge the burden of establishing the risk required under the first prong of the IFA test

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants' fear hypothetical and agrees with RPD that appellants failed to prove risk under first prong of IFA test.

propositions.text: Evidence does not show serious possibility of persecution or risk to life or torture in proposed Mexican states under first prong of IFA test
propositions.quote: the evidence presented does not show that there is a serious possibility of persecution for the appellants or that there is a probability that they would be subjected to a risk to their life, a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or torture if they were to settle in one of the proposed states in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no serious possibility of persecution or risk to life or torture in proposed Mexican states under first prong of IFA test.

propositions.text: RPD found appellants' concerns were agents finding them and employment difficulties for principal and female associate appellants
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the appellants simply raised the following concerns: that the agents of persecution would find them and that the principal appellant and female associate appellant would not be able to find employment

propositions.text: RPD noted appellants had always worked in Mexico and US (principal appellant)
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the appellants had always worked in Mexico and the United States (for the principal appellant)

propositions.text: RPD concluded appellants could resettle, find work and meet needs in Campeche or Yucatan
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RPD concluded that the appellants would all be able to resettle elsewhere, find work and meet their needs, whether it be in Campeche or in Yucatan

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellants' concerns about agents and employment but concluded they could resettle and find work in Campeche or Yucatan.

propositions.text: Appellants argue no family or friends support in suggested areas
propositions.quote: They do not have any family members or friends in the areas suggested so they will not have any support in relocating to those areas

propositions.text: Appellants argue they are just a taxi driver and a woman without education
propositions.quote: They are just a taxi driver and a woman without any education

propositions.text: Appellants argue they had jobs in cities with family and friends support
propositions.quote: They had jobs in cities where they had support from family and friends

propositions.text: Appellants argue job situation in Mexico should not be compared to US
propositions.quote: The job situation in Mexico should not be compared to that in the United States

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue lack of support, limited education, prior jobs with support, and that Mexico's job situation differs from the US.

propositions.text: Removal to unfamiliar city will be very distressing
propositions.quote: The appellants submit that their removal to an unfamiliar city will be very distressing for them

paragraphs.summary: The appellants submit removal to an unfamiliar city will cause them great distress.

propositions.text: The RAD cannot agree with appellants' arguments and finds them unfounded
propositions.quote: The RAD cannot agree with the appellants' arguments and concludes that they are unfounded

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellants' arguments unfounded and disagrees with them.

propositions.text: High threshold for unreasonableness of IFA requires proof of adverse conditions jeopardizing life and safety
propositions.quote: there is a very high threshold for what makes an IFA unreasonable, considering the particular circumstances. This high standard requires proof of adverse conditions which would jeopardize the life and safety of the claimant in travelling to and in living in the IFA location

paragraphs.summary: Case law sets a high threshold for unreasonableness of IFA, requiring proof of adverse conditions jeopardizing life and safety.

propositions.text: Immigration forms establish appellants' occupations sufficiently
propositions.quote: The immigration forms of each appellant are sufficient to establish their respective occupations

propositions.text: Principal appellant is taxi driver, wife worked in restaurant industry, son can find job
propositions.quote: The principal appellant is a taxi driver, his wife has always been able to work in the restaurant industry, and her son testified that he would be able to find a job

propositions.text: All appellants speak Spanish, the language used in proposed areas
propositions.quote: All of them speak Spanish, which is the language used in the proposed areas

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants' occupations and Spanish language skills sufficient for proposed areas.

propositions.text: RPD did not compare employment situations in US and Mexico
propositions.quote: the RPD did not compare the employment situation in the two countries

propositions.text: RPD noted principal appellant worked in Mexico and US
propositions.quote: It simply noted that the principal appellant had always worked, both in Mexico and during his stay in the United States

paragraphs.summary: The court clarifies RPD did not compare US and Mexico employment but noted principal appellant's work history in both.

propositions.text: Principal appellant indicated willingness to do any employment if refugee claim allowed
propositions.quote: On his immigration form (IMM0008), the principal appellant indicated [translation] "Anything" for the type of employment he would do if his claim for refugee protection in Canada was allowed

propositions.text: Associate appellants indicated willingness to do any reasonable employment
propositions.quote: The associate appellants both indicated [translation] "any reasonable employment" on their forms

paragraphs.summary: Immigration forms show appellants' willingness to accept any or reasonable employment if refugee claim allowed.

propositions.text: Claim that removal would cause distress and inability to find liked job does not meet high threshold of second prong of IFA test
propositions.quote: The claim that it would be unreasonable for the appellants to seek refuge in the proposed IFAs because it would cause them great distress and they would not be able to find a job they like does not meet the high threshold of the second prong of the IFA test

paragraphs.summary: The court finds distress and job preference claims do not meet the high threshold of the second prong of the IFA test.

propositions.text: It is not about claimant's convenience or attractiveness of IFA; burden is to prove jeopardy to life or safety
propositions.quote: It is not a matter of the claimant's convenience or the attractiveness of the IFA. The appellants had to establish on a balance of probabilities that the IFA would jeopardize their lives or safety

paragraphs.summary: The court states the IFA test requires proof of jeopardy to life or safety, not convenience or attractiveness.

propositions.text: RPD concluded appellants did not establish objective unreasonableness of seeking refuge in proposed cities
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the appellants [translation] "did not establish that it would be objectively unreasonable for them to seek refuge in these cities, given the conditions in the proposed cities and all of the circumstances in this case, including their personal circumstances

propositions.text: The RAD agrees with RPD's conclusion that appellants failed to establish objective unreasonableness
propositions.quote: The RAD agrees. The RPD's conclusion is correct

paragraphs.summary: The RPD concluded appellants failed to prove objective unreasonableness; the RAD agrees with this conclusion.

propositions.text: RPD's decision is correct; appellants failed to show errors justifying RAD intervention
propositions.quote: The RPD's decision is correct. Consequently, considering all of the above, the RAD concludes that the appellants have failed to demonstrate that the RDP committed errors that would justify the RAD's intervention

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD decision is correct and appellants failed to show errors justifying intervention.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD's determination appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA
propositions.quote: the RAD confirms the RPD's determination, namely that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are not "Convention refugees" under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) or "persons in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal.
